thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: smart-routing policy 'fast-switchover-v2' is reporting >5% error-rate AND >20% fallback rate across us-west1 -> eu-west1 in the last 2m. paging oncall @alex (pager duty)
alex (oncall): acked. looking. seeing a lot of 500s labeled 'variant-mismatch' from router logs. can ppl join? :eyes:
maya (sre): joining. grep is showing repetitive route flips between eu-west1 and us-west1 for session-id prefixes. looks like sticky fallback TTL isn't expiring fast enough, transactions keep getting pinned to failing variant.
dan (infra): I can tail the routing-policy logs. policy engine shows a recent config push 5m ago: policy=fast-switchover-v2, fallback=sticky-variant, fallback-ttl=600s, allow-variant=redwood-llm-v2-q4, canary-variant=redwood-llm-v2-alpha. that alpha variant is throwing inference errors (nan outputs) under longer sequences.
priya (runtime): confirmed. alpha has a regression in kv-cache handling; returns 500s for seq>2048. Canary was supposed to be 10% traffic but sticky fallback pins sessions to alpha after a fallback and TTL is long — we're seeing oscillation when alpha fails then sticky keeps pinning subsequent requests.
sam (support): we're seeing ~120 customer-facing errors across a handful of high-volume customers. CS started inbound threads. Priority customers flagged. moving to incident.
emily (product): what's the customer impact scope? percent of requests and are embeddings affected?
maya (sre): approx 3.2% of total requests, concentrated on chat endpoints and a few dedicated customers using session affinity. embeddings endpoints unaffected.
alex (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) pause the canary rollout 2) disable sticky fallback for policy fast-switchover-v2 3) emergency route override to stable variant redwood-llm-v1 for affected regions. I'll execute with approvals.
priya (runtime): agree. to disable sticky quickly we can set policy flag `sticky: false` in the policy store (Redis key: policy:fast-switchover-v2). Dan can you flip? I'll monitor the runtime for KV cache churn.
dan (infra): running now: ```
# disable sticky fallback
redis-cli -h routing-store GET policy:fast-switchover-v2
redis-cli -h routing-store HSET policy:fast-switchover-v2 sticky false
# confirm
redis-cli -h routing-store HGET policy:fast-switchover-v2 sticky
```
infra-bot: CMD_OK: HSET succeeded. policy:fast-switchover-v2.sticky=false
alex (oncall): next step override routes in route-fence for us-west1/eu-west1 to redwood-llm-v1 (stable) for 15m. Dan—can you apply route-fence? Use `routectl`.
dan (infra): applying override: ```
routectl set-override --policy fast-switchover-v2 --region us-west1 --variant redwood-llm-v1 --ttl 900
routectl set-override --policy fast-switchover-v2 --region eu-west1 --variant redwood-llm-v1 --ttl 900
``` infra-bot: OVERRIDE_APPLIED for both regions
maya (sre): monitoring metrics... fallback rate dropping, error-rate trending down. sessions are no longer bouncing between regions. latency stable. keeping metrics window open for 10m.
priya (runtime): note: disabling sticky will increase cold KV cache misses for a bit but should avoid repeated hits to alpha. I'll watch memory and cache eviction.
sam (support): sending customer update: "We've applied temporary routing to a stable model and paused the canary. We expect reduced errors within minutes. We'll follow up with postmortem." cc: affected customers
emily (product): thanks. capture which customers had pinned sessions so we can offer remediation credits if needed.
alex (oncall): canary paused: I rolled back canary flag in rollout-service: ```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://rollout.internal/api/pause -d '{"rollout":"fast-switchover-v2"}'
``` response: 200 OK
maya (sre): metrics now show fallbacks <1% and request errors dropped to baseline. keeping elevated watch for 30m. good to reduce paging if stable in 15m.
priya (runtime): root cause hypothesis: canary variant redwood-llm-v2-alpha has a regression under long sequences resulting in 500s; policy's sticky fallback TTL was too long (600s) which allowed sessions to be repeatedly pinned to the bad variant after fallbacks, creating a loop when smart router tried region fallback -> sticky pinned -> canary -> fail.
alex (oncall): next actions: - leave route overrides in place for 15m - shorten fallback-ttl to 30s for safe default - add a policy validation that rejects sticky=true if fallback-ttl>300s (proposal) - postmortem owner: maya
maya (sre): putting a quick hotfix: ```
redis-cli -h routing-store HSET policy:fast-switchover-v2 fallback-ttl 30
``` infra-bot: HSET succeeded. fallback-ttl=30
dan (infra): also adding a dev-alert rule: if variant-error-rate > 2% for >1m during canary, auto-pause rollout. I'll file PR for rollout-service auto-pause.
alex (oncall): support: please send updated message to customers after 30m confirming resolution. Sam to coordinate.
sam (support): will do. drafted message and waiting for final confirm.
emily (product): please attach which model artifacts were promoted to alpha. priya, can you collect model commit hash and provenance for the canary build?
priya (runtime): canary artifact: git sha=ab12f3c, build=ci/2026-03-14-18:22. I'll upload logs to the incident doc and snapshot model outputs showing NaN sequences.
maya (sre): assigning postmortem owner: maya. I'll create the postmortem doc, include timeline, mitigations, and follow-ups. adding action items: check policy validator, rollout auto-pause, fallback TTL health-checks.
alex (oncall): demobilizing paging in ~20m if stable. thanks everyone for quick responses :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (sticky disabled, route override, canary paused). severity downgraded to SEV3. monitoring continues.
alex (oncall): last note — let's avoid immediate full rollback of model repo until runtime team confirms KV fix. prefer repro and small fix then canary re-run with stricter guardrails.
priya (runtime): agreed. I'll try to reproduce locally, then coordinate a guarded canary when fixed.
sam (support): customer message sent: "We've applied a temporary routing fix and paused the canary. We'll follow up with details and an ETA for remediation." recipients: 4 enterprise customers.
emily (product): add customer impact to postmortem and estimate credit exposure.
maya (sre): last_message: metrics stable for 12m, closing paging. follow-ups tracked in incident doc. postmortem owner: maya.
